question: Should queued webhook ingestion become a core Gateway feature through this hooks.queues plus SQLite/RPC/UI design, and what public protocol contract must ship with it?
rationale: This PR creates new core config, durable state, HTTP ingress, advertised Gateway RPCs, and UI behavior, so automation should not settle the product/API boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Review Core Queue Design
options.body: Proceed with this PR after adding protocol schemas/validators and maintainer-reviewed upgrade and permission proof.

options.title: Narrow To Runtime Lane
options.body: Defer durable queue storage/UI and solve the immediate burst problem through a smaller hook concurrency lane or session admission change.

options.title: Defer From Core
options.body: Keep immediate hooks as the core path until a plugin/API extension or stronger operator demand justifies durable core queues.

recommendation.title: Review Core Queue Design
recommendation.body: Proceed with this PR after adding protocol schemas/validators and maintainer-reviewed upgrade and permission proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Gateway hook, state, and Control UI history makes this the best available owner for the core API/product shape decision.
